2610.02684.title: Large language models exhibit unreliable updating of clinical judgment as patient evidence evolves
2610.02684.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored for clinical reasoning, but whether they appropriately revise judgments as patient evidence evolves remains unclear. We evaluated longitudinal belief updating using matched intensive-care trajectories from electronic health records. Across diverse LLMs, conditioning on a preceding judgment more often increased than reduced prediction error when estimates changed, replicated for a second endpoint. Controlled interventions revealed two failure modes. First, with preceding assessment fixed, models responded more strongly to worsening than matched improving respiratory evidence; this asymmetry persisted after headroom normalization at moderate and strong evidence levels. Second, with current evidence fixed, increasing prior risk from 10% to 90% shifted estimates by 26.2 percentage points, demonstrating causal influence of prior model beliefs. Prompting did not restore reliable updating. Evidence-Validated Longitudinal Update (EVLU) identified fewer, more reliable revisions, revealing a reliability-coverage trade-off. These findings establish longitudinal belief updating as a distinct dimension of LLM reliability.
2610.02684.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）在臨床推理中越來越受到關注，但隨著患者證據的演變，它們是否能適當地修正判斷仍然不清楚。<lb/>我們使用來自電子健康紀錄的匹配重症監護軌跡評估了長期信念更新。<lb/>在多樣的LLMs中，當估計值發生變化時，基於先前判斷的條件下，增加預測誤差的情況比減少的情況更為常見，這一結果在第二個端點中得到了重複。<lb/>受控干預揭示了兩種失敗模式。<lb/>首先，在固定先前評估的情況下，模型對於惡化的呼吸證據的反應比對於匹配的改善呼吸證據的反應更強烈；這種不對稱性在中等和強證據水平的頭部空間標準化後仍然存在。<lb/>其次，在固定當前證據的情況下，將先前風險從10%提高到90%使估計值變動了26.2個百分點，顯示了先前模型信念的因果影響。<lb/>提示並未恢復可靠的更新。<lb/>證據驗證的長期更新（EVLU）識別出較少且更可靠的修訂，揭示了可靠性與覆蓋範圍之間的權衡。<lb/>這些發現確立了長期信念更新作為LLM可靠性的獨特維度。
